rationale: Evidence: 17 of 20 oval trials and all 40 s-bend and slalom trials ended off track, with max_error at 0.06 m, the off-track limit for this body (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06 m). Line-loss events were about 1 per run, and progress was only 0.17 on the s-bend and 0.12 on the slalom. The robot loses the line on bends and never recovers. Likely causes: (a) the sensor span of 0.08 m (x = ±0.04) is barely wider than the 0.025 m tape plus the turning lag, so on sharp bends the tape leaves the array; (b) kp = 2.5 with kd = 0.3 corrects too slowly at 1.5 base speed, and the robot runs wide before the correction builds; (c) the sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the wheels reach the tape before the sensors have fully corrected. Changes: widen the array to x = ±0.07 m (5 sensors, 0.035 m spacing) so the line stays under a sensor through tighter bends; move the array forward to y = 0.06 m for more lead; raise kp to 3.5 for stronger correction; raise kd to 0.6 to damp the extra gain; lower base_speed to 1.3 to give the controller time to respond on bends, at a small cost in completion time. Keep ki = 0 to avoid integral windup, and keep line_loss = last_direction. Expected result: fewer off-track ends on the s-bend and slalom, with progress above 0.5 on those tracks and a finish on the oval. Hypotheses to test next: (1) widening the span reduces line_loss_events to near 0; (2) steering_oscillation stays below about 0.4 at kp 3.5 and kd 0.6; (3) completion time rises by about 0.1 to 0.2 s from the lower base speed, which is acceptable if completion rate rises. Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, max_error and line_loss_events, which will show whether the failure is line loss or steering lag.
